name: Kolkata
tagline: Colonial grandeur, Bengali arts and unhurried intellectual soul.
whenBlurb: The cool, dry winter from November to February is the city at its finest, crowned by October's Durga Puja; sidestep the sticky summer and the July-to-September monsoon.

ourTake.lede: Kolkata is India's most literary and soulful big city, and it rewards walking, conversation and coffee-house afternoons more than any monument checklist. Do the colonial core and the north-Kolkata lanes with a good guide, give real time to the food and the sweet shops, and, if you possibly can, time your visit to Durga Puja. Skip the rush; the city's pleasure is in lingering.
ourTake.comeIf: You want the most literary, coffee-house city in India and its extraordinary food.
ourTake.skipIf: You want polish, beaches or nightlife.

guide.lede: Where to stay, what to do, where to eat, and where the night goes, grouped by price, every address earned by a name worth trusting.

items.name: The Oberoi Grand, Kolkata
credentials: Forbes Traveler 400, Best Hotels & Resorts in the World (2008, 2009)
INTACH Blue Cultural Plaque (2024), heritage recognition as the 'Grande Dame of Chowringhee'
items.description: The 'Grande Dame of Chowringhee', a colonnaded 1880s landmark and the definitive luxury address in the city for over a century.

items.name: Taj Bengal, Kolkata
credentials: National Tourism Award, Best Luxury Hotel, Eastern Region (1998)
IHCL / Taj Hotels, recognised at Condé Nast Traveller Readers' Travel Awards (group)
items.description: The Taj's leafy Alipore flagship since 1989, a grand atrium house in the city's most gracious residential quarter.

items.name: ITC Royal Bengal, a Luxury Collection Hotel, Kolkata
credentials: Marriott Luxury Collection
BW Hotelier Indian Hospitality Awards 2025, General Manager, Luxury (East)
items.description: A vast LEED-Platinum modern palace and the newest apex hotel in the city, Bengal grandeur at scale.

items.name: JW Marriott Hotel Kolkata
items.area: CBD-adjacent (JBS Haldane Avenue, near Science City)
credentials: Marriott JW Marriott brand, luxury tier
Recognised award-winning Spa by JW
items.description: A polished contemporary JW with a striking infinity pool, the sharp business-and-wedding house on the eastern flank.

items.name: The Park Kolkata
credentials: Travel + Leisure India, Best Business Hotel in India (2020)
The Park Hotels, India's pioneering boutique-design group
items.description: India's original design hotel and the beating heart of Park Street nightlife, four bars and clubs under one roof.

items.name: ITC Sonar, Kolkata
credentials: ITC Hotels, responsible-luxury flagship (LEED Platinum)
Houses West View & Dum Pukht Kolkata, ITC signature dining
items.description: A garden-and-water resort within the city, lagoon-set lawns, a celebrated spa, and one of India's greenest luxury hotels.

items.name: Taj Taj City Centre New Town, Kolkata
items.area: New Town / Rajarhat (near the airport & IT corridor)
credentials: IHCL / Taj Hotels, luxury group standing
items.description: A crisp, contemporary Taj beside the New Town business district, the practical modern-Taj option near the airport.

items.name: Victoria Memorial Hall
items.description: The great white Makrana-marble monument the British raised to their Empress, its Indo-Saracenic dome floating above the Maidan's lawns. Twenty-five galleries hold the finest collection of Raj-era paintings and Kolkata's own history; come at dusk when it glows and the reflecting pools double it.

items.name: The Maidan
items.description: Kolkata's vast green lung, a mile of parkland running from Fort William to Park Street where the whole city comes to breathe, jog, play cricket and fly kites. A morning walk here, past grazing horses and hand-pulled tea sellers, is the truest way to feel the city's rhythm.

items.name: St Paul's Cathedral
items.description: The first purpose-built Anglican cathedral in Asia, all soaring Gothic Revival white and stained glass by Burne-Jones. A cool, hushed contrast a two-minute walk from the Victoria Memorial, and a lovely place to sit for a moment away from the heat.

items.name: Indian Museum
items.description: The oldest and largest museum in India, founded in 1814, a colonnaded treasure house of Gandhara sculpture, the Bharhut stupa railings, Egyptian mummies and Mughal miniatures. The building itself, wrapped around a grand courtyard, is worth the visit for architecture lovers travelling with children.

items.name: Howrah Bridge (Rabindra Setu)
items.description: The steel cantilever colossus that has carried Kolkata across the Hooghly since 1943, one of the busiest bridges on earth and the city's defining silhouette. Best seen at first light from the Mullick Ghat flower market beneath it, where garlands pile up in colour.

items.name: Hooghly River cruise
items.description: A slow boat down the Hooghly threads together the ghats, the two great bridges, Belur Math and the colonial river frontage in one unhurried afternoon. Sunset sailings with tea and Bengali snacks are the most civilised way to watch the city's skyline turn gold.

items.name: Marble Palace
items.description: A private 1835 mansion of a Bengali aristocrat, packed floor to ceiling with Italian marble, Belgian chandeliers, Rubens and Reynolds canvases and a menagerie in its garden. Still owned by the Mullick family; a permit and a guide are needed, which keeps it wonderfully untouristed.

items.name: Kumartuli idol-makers' quarter
items.description: The warren of riverside workshops where generations of sculptors shape the clay Durga and Kali idols for the whole city's festivals. In the weeks before Durga Puja the lanes are thick with straw armatures and wet earth; a photographer's dream and a living craft, not a museum.

items.name: Kalighat Kali Temple
items.description: The 19th-century shrine that gave Calcutta its name, one of the 51 Shakti Peethas and the spiritual heart of the city's devotion to the goddess. Intense, crowded and deeply alive; a guide will help you navigate the queues and understand what you are seeing.

items.name: Dakshineswar Kali Temple
items.description: Rani Rashmoni's grand nine-spired temple on the Hooghly, where the mystic Ramakrishna served as priest and had his visions. The riverside setting and the twelve Shiva shrines along the bank make it far more serene than Kalighat; note that phones and cameras are not allowed inside.

items.name: Belur Math
items.description: The riverside headquarters of the Ramakrishna Mission, whose extraordinary temple deliberately fuses Hindu, Islamic, Buddhist and Christian architecture into one form. The vast, calm gardens on the Hooghly are among the most peaceful spaces near the city; pair it by ferry with Dakshineswar opposite.

items.name: Mother House (Missionaries of Charity)
items.description: The simple headquarters of Mother Teresa's order, where her plain tomb and small museum room draw quiet pilgrims from across the world. An unadorned, moving stop that puts the city's charitable spirit in front of you.

items.name: College Street book bazaar (Boi Para)
items.description: A kilometre of pavement stacked with new, old and rare books, said to be the largest second-hand book market in the world and the intellectual soul of Bengal. Browse for a first edition, then do as the students do and disappear into the coffee house for adda.

items.name: Indian Coffee House, College Street
items.description: The high-ceilinged, faded hall where poets, filmmakers and revolutionaries have argued over infinite cups since the 1940s, the very cradle of Bengali adda. The coffee is ordinary and the conversation is the point; sit under the fans and let time slow.

items.name: Park Street
items.description: Kolkata's grand old boulevard of jazz, cabarets and legendary restaurants, still lined with institutions like Flurys, Trincas and Mocambo. It blazes with lights at Christmas and stays the city's most nostalgic address for a long, unhurried dinner.

items.name: South Park Street Cemetery
items.description: A hauntingly beautiful garden of 1,600 crumbling Georgian tombs, obelisks and pyramids overgrown with roots, one of the oldest non-church European cemeteries anywhere. An atmospheric, photogenic hour reading the epitaphs of the young Britons who never made it home.

items.name: BBD Bagh (Dalhousie Square) colonial core
items.description: The old imperial heart, where the East India Company ran an empire from a square of magnificent buildings around a central tank. Walk it slowly to read Kolkata as the second city of the British Empire, block by grand block.

items.name: Writers' Building
items.description: The long red pile that housed the clerks ('writers') of the East India Company and later the seat of Bengal's government, its facade one of the most recognisable in the city. Best admired from the square outside, a monument to Company rule.

items.name: General Post Office (GPO)
items.description: A soaring domed rotunda on the site of the original Fort William, marking the very spot of the infamous Black Hole of Calcutta. Its Corinthian columns and philatelic museum make it a rewarding pause on any Dalhousie heritage walk.

items.name: Town Hall (Kolkata)
items.description: A restored Roman-Doric grand hall of 1813, now home to an engaging museum on the city's own story told through light, sound and models. A polished, air-conditioned introduction to Kolkata's history for a first-time or multi-generation visit.

items.name: Prinsep Ghat
items.description: A graceful Palladian riverside pavilion of 1841 beneath the Vidyasagar Setu cable-stayed bridge, and the prettiest stretch of Kolkata's waterfront. Come for the sunset, a short boat ride, and the promenade that fills with families in the cool of the evening.

items.name: Eden Gardens & Test cricket
items.description: One of the oldest and most storied cricket grounds on earth, a cauldron of 65,000 voices when India play under lights. Even on a quiet day the ground carries the weight of legendary matches; catching a fixture here is a bucket-list experience for the cricket-loving family.

items.name: New Market (Hogg Market)
items.description: The rambling Victorian covered bazaar of 1874, a labyrinth of over 2,000 stalls selling everything from cheese and cold cuts to fabric, flowers and silver. Nahoum's, the century-old Jewish bakery inside, is the reason many still make the pilgrimage.

items.name: Tiretti Bazaar Chinese breakfast
items.description: At dawn on the lanes of old Chinatown, the last families of Kolkata's Chinese community sell momos, pork buns, fish-ball soup and rice-noodle rolls from steaming carts. A vanishing ritual worth setting an early alarm for; go on a Sunday when it is busiest.

items.name: Jorasanko Thakur Bari (Tagore House)
items.description: The rambling ancestral mansion where Rabindranath Tagore was born, wrote much of his work and died, now a beautifully kept museum to the family that shaped modern Bengal. Essential for anyone who loves literature and the Bengal Renaissance, set in an evocative old-city quarter.

items.name: Academy of Fine Arts
items.description: Kolkata's leading gallery and theatre complex beside the Rabindra Sadan cultural district, home to changing exhibitions and a permanent Tagore collection. The best single stop to take the pulse of the city's contemporary art and stage life.

items.name: Kolkata tram ride
items.description: Asia's oldest operating tram network, running since 1902, still trundles a handful of heritage routes through the old city at a gloriously unhurried pace. A joyride on a wooden-slatted carriage past Esplanade is a nostalgic pleasure that is slowly disappearing.

items.name: Durga Puja pandal-hopping
credentials: UNESCO Intangible Cultural Heritage of Humanity
items.description: For five days each autumn the whole city becomes an open-air gallery of themed pandals, some the size of cathedrals, each an artwork built to be dissolved in the river. It is Kolkata at its most joyous and unmissable; the festival is inscribed on UNESCO's list of intangible cultural heritage.

items.name: Kalighat Pat painting & patuas
items.description: The bold, quick-brushed folk paintings born in the temple bazaars of the 19th century, a distinctly Kolkata art form now prized by collectors. Seek them out near the temple and in city galleries; an original pat is a meaningful thing to take home.

items.name: Park Street kathi rolls & street food
items.description: The kathi roll, an egg-coated paratha wrapped around spiced kebab, was invented at Nizam's near New Market and is Kolkata's great gift to street food. Eating one hot off the griddle, then a phuchka from a roadside cart, is a rite of passage in this most food-obsessed of Indian cities.

items.name: Bengali sweets crawl
items.description: The city that gave the world the rosogolla still treats sweet-making as high art, from the syrup-soaked chhena of Balaram Mullick to the nolen gur mishti doi of winter. A morning tasting your way through the century-old sweet shops is pure, delicious Bengal.

items.name: Kolkata coffee-house adda
items.description: Adda, the unhurried art of conversation for its own sake, is Bengal's greatest institution, practised over endless cups in coffee houses and para rooftops. To be drawn into an adda is to be let into the real city; nowhere in India talks quite like Kolkata.

items.name: Nakhoda Masjid & Zakaria Street
items.description: The city's largest mosque, a red-sandstone echo of Akbar's tomb, presides over the fragrant Muslim quarter of Zakaria Street. In Ramadan the lanes below turn into one of India's great night food markets, heavy with haleem, kebabs and firni.

items.name: Paresnath Jain Temple (Shitalnath)
items.description: A dazzling 1867 Jain temple encrusted with mirrors, Belgian glass, Venetian mosaics and coloured stones set in a fountain garden. One of the most ornate and least-visited jewels in the city, and a serene surprise in the busy north.

items.name: Rabindra Sarobar & the Lakes
items.description: A tranquil man-made lake ringed by walking paths, rowing clubs and old trees, where south Kolkata comes to jog, row and do sunrise yoga. A green, breathable counterpoint to the crowded old city, and lovely early in the morning.

items.name: Victoria Memorial sound-and-light show
items.description: As night falls, the monument's own history and that of the city are narrated across its lit facade in an evening spectacle in the gardens. A gentle, atmospheric way to end a day, especially with children in tow.

items.name: Kumortuli to Sovabazar heritage walk
items.description: The lanes of old north Kolkata hide crumbling merchant mansions (rajbaris), hidden thakur-dalans and the courtyards where Durga Puja began. A guided morning walk here peels back the aristocratic Bengal that built the city, layer by layer.

items.name: Mullick Ghat flower market
items.description: One of Asia's largest wholesale flower markets sprawls under the Howrah Bridge, a riot of marigold garlands, lotus and roses from before dawn. Arrive at sunrise for extraordinary photographs of colour, chaos and the great steel bridge above.

items.name: Metropolitan Building & Esplanade colonial walk
items.description: The restored, cream-and-red Metropolitan (Whiteaway Laidlaw) building anchors a stretch of grand old department stores and colonial facades around Chowringhee. A rewarding architecture stroll that ends naturally at New Market or the Grand.

items.name: The Oberoi Grand high tea
items.description: The 'Grande Dame of Chowringhee', a colonial-era hotel whose colonnaded courtyard has hosted the city's grandest occasions for over a century. Even if you stay elsewhere, afternoon tea beneath its arches is a graceful way to touch old Calcutta.

items.name: Sundarbans day trip
credentials: UNESCO World Heritage Site
items.description: The world's largest mangrove forest and the tiger-haunted delta where the Ganges meets the sea, best explored slowly by launch through its tidal creeks. A UNESCO World Heritage Site and biosphere reserve; a night on a boat is far better than a rushed day, but even a day gives you the wild edge of Bengal.

items.name: Shantiniketan day trip
items.description: Tagore's serene university town where classes are still held under the trees and the whole ethos is art, nature and simplicity. Visit the ashram, the Kala Bhavana art school and the Saturday tribal craft market; the winter Poush Mela is magical.

items.name: Bishnupur terracotta temples day trip
items.description: The old Malla capital is studded with 17th-century temples whose brick walls are carved edge to edge with terracotta scenes from the epics, unlike anything else in India. Pair the Rasmancha and Jor Bangla temples with a Baluchari silk saree bought at its source.

items.name: Chandannagar day trip
items.description: A former French colony on the Hooghly with a genuinely Gallic riverfront promenade, a domed church and the elegant Dupleix mansion museum. A charming half-day of European Bengal, at its most dazzling during its famous Jagaddhatri Puja illuminations.

items.name: Chinsurah & Bandel Church day trip
items.description: The Hooghly's old colonial river-towns layer Portuguese, Dutch and Danish history within an hour of the city, crowned by the 1599 Bandel Basilica, one of the oldest churches in Bengal. A quiet, offbeat outing for travellers who like their history undiscovered.

items.name: Bohemian
credentials: Condé Nast Traveller India x Zomato Top Restaurant Awards 2024, No. 41 in India
items.description: Chef Joymalya Banerjee's modern-Bengali table, traditional spices and ingredients pushed into unexpected, playful territory.

items.name: Baan Thai
credentials: Condé Nast Traveller India x Zomato Top Restaurant Awards 2024, No. 27 in India
items.description: The Oberoi Grand's long-loved Thai room, teak, silk and precise, refined cooking above Chowringhee.

items.name: 6 Ballygunge Place
credentials: Landmark Kolkata Bengali fine-dining institution, regarded among the city's best for authentic Bengali cuisine (Incredible India, Culture Trip)
items.description: Bengali fine dining in a restored 1930s mansion, slow-cooked royal-Bengal curries in the city's most gracious dining house.

items.name: Oh! Calcutta
credentials: Landmark restaurant credited with popularising Bengali fine dining nationally (Speciality Restaurants, recognised group)
items.description: The restaurant that carried Bengali cuisine across India, comforting fish curries and melt-in-the-mouth mutton in a warm room.

items.name: West View
credentials: Inside ITC Sonar, ITC Hotels signature dining
items.description: ITC Sonar's grill-and-fine-dining room, a polished western table for members who want a hotel-standard dinner near the CBD.

items.name: Kewpie's Kitchen
credentials: Legendary family-run Kolkata institution, regarded among the city's best for home-style Bengali cuisine (India.com, Culture Trip)
items.description: A family home turned dining room, authentic Bengali cooking from recipes handed down through the Dasgupta family.

items.name: Peter Cat
credentials: TasteAtlas, 150 Most Legendary Restaurants in the World (2023), ranked No. 17
items.description: The Park Street icon since 1975, home of the Chelo Kebab, rice and kebabs under a poached egg, a Kolkata institution unto itself.

items.name: Mocambo
credentials: Condé Nast Traveller India x Zomato Top Restaurant Awards 2024, No. 37 in India
Kolkata heritage-restaurant status, Park Street institution
items.description: A 1956 continental time-capsule, Devil Crab, sizzlers and Anglo-Italian classics under the same neon since the fifties.

items.name: Kwality
items.area: Park Street area (17 Park Street / Free School Street)
credentials: Kolkata heritage-restaurant status, Park Street institution
items.description: One of Park Street's grand old continental-and-Mughlai rooms, chelo, kebabs and dal that have fed the city for generations.

items.name: Arsalan
credentials: Landmark Kolkata biryani institution, the city's best-known Kolkata biryani (est. 2002; Tripadvisor top-ranked biryani)
items.description: Kolkata's most famous biryani house, the fragrant, potato-and-egg Kolkata biryani that defines the city's Mughlai table.

items.name: Flurys
credentials: Heritage Park Street institution since 1927, Kolkata's most storied tearoom
items.description: The 1927 Park Street tearoom, a Raj-era confectionery of pastries, rum balls and English breakfasts, unchanged in spirit.

items.name: Nizam's
credentials: Heritage institution, credited as the birthplace of the Kolkata Kathi Roll (est. 1930s)
items.description: The birthplace of the Kathi Roll, kebabs rolled in a paratha, invented here in the 1930s and still served hot to order.

items.name: Trincas
credentials: Historic Park Street live-music institution since 1959
The enduring heart of Kolkata's jazz-and-cabaret nightlife
items.description: Park Street's legendary listening room, live music every night since 1959, the stage that launched Usha Uthup.

items.name: The Chowringhee Bar
credentials: Named Best Bar/Pub, The Times Food Guide, The Times of India (2004)
Inside The Oberoi Grand, INTACH heritage-recognised (2024)
items.description: The Oberoi Grand's clubby colonial bar, dark wood, single malts and the quietest, most grown-up nightcap in the city.

items.name: Roxy
credentials: Inside The Park Kolkata, India's pioneering design-hotel group
Recognised Park Street cocktail-and-wine destination
items.description: A witty, design-led cocktail-and-wine bar channelling the swinging sixties, the most stylish drinking room on Park Street.

items.name: Someplace Else
credentials: Pioneering Indian live-music pub, the brand that took Kolkata nightlife national
Inside The Park Kolkata, Travel + Leisure India Best Business Hotel (2020)
items.description: India's original live-band pub, the loud, joyful rock room that has defined Kolkata's pub culture for three decades.

plan.heading: 4 days in Kolkata, done well
plan.lede: A day-by-day shape for the trip, the pace we would set. Your advisor books the flights and the rooms; the days are yours.

slots.label: Morning
slots.text: The Victoria Memorial and the Maidan in the morning, then St. Paul's Cathedral nearby.

slots.label: Afternoon
slots.text: The Indian Museum and a slow walk down the colonnades of the old central business quarter.

slots.label: Evening
slots.text: Dinner at the Bengali table of 6 Ballygunge Place, or Kewpie's home-style thali.

slots.label: Morning
slots.text: The lanes of Kumartuli where the idol-makers work in clay, then Marble Palace.

slots.label: Afternoon
slots.text: The Howrah bridge and a boat on the Hooghly past the ghats at dusk.

slots.label: Evening
slots.text: Kathi rolls at Nizam's, or a proper dinner at Oh! Calcutta.

slots.label: Morning
slots.text: College Street's book market and the Indian Coffee House, then the Ashutosh museum.

slots.label: Afternoon
slots.text: The Rabindra Bharati house-museum at Jorasanko, Tagore's family home.

slots.label: Evening
slots.text: A cultural evening, then dinner at The Bridge in the Taj Bengal.

slots.label: Morning
slots.text: A morning of Bengali sweets, sandesh and mishti doi from a century-old shop like Balaram Mullick.

slots.label: Afternoon
slots.text: The Belur Math and the Dakshineswar temple across the river.

slots.label: Evening
slots.text: A final Bengali dinner before departure, or club dinner at the Tollygunge.

items.name: Park Street / Camac Street
items.description: The central heart of dining, clubs and colonial hotels; best for comfort and city access.

items.name: North Kolkata (Shobhabazar, College Street)
items.description: The old city of mansions, book lanes and the coffee house; suits heritage and atmosphere.

items.name: Alipore / Ballygunge
items.description: The leafy, gracious residential south; for a quiet, upscale base among old bungalows.

events.name: Durga Puja
events.note: The city's defining festival, a UNESCO-recognised explosion of art, devotion and street life; the single best time to visit.

events.name: Kali Puja & Diwali
events.note: A dramatic night of goddess worship and lights following close on Durga Puja.

events.name: Kolkata International Film Festival
events.note: A major, long-running film festival that fills the city's cinemas and its intellectual life.

events.name: Poush Mela / Christmas season
events.note: Park Street's famous Christmas lights and the nearby Santiniketan Poush Mela make December especially lively.

onGround.heading: On the ground
onGround.note: Stay around Park Street, Alipore or the Victoria Memorial for the best of old Calcutta; the city is at its most beautiful and social during Durga Puja in autumn, though it books out early; the coffee houses, sweet shops and colonial architecture reward an unhurried pace.

rows.label: Arriving
rows.value: Fly into Netaji Subhas Chandra Bose international airport and take a private chauffeur into town; the airport is in the north, roughly forty-five minutes to an hour from the central and south Kolkata hotels.

rows.label: Getting around
rows.value: A private car and driver is the sensible way to navigate the traffic, though the colonial core around Park Street and the Maidan is a rewarding walk, and a heritage tram or river ferry makes a fine occasional detour.

rows.label: Connectivity
rows.value: Reliable 4G and 5G across the city on all networks; eSIMs and hotel wifi are dependable.

rows.label: Money
rows.value: Indian rupee; cards and UPI are widely taken, with cash handy for old bookshops, sweet shops and markets; ten percent is a gracious tip.

rows.label: Climate
rows.value: November–February is the kind season: dry, mild and at its cultural best around Durga Puja's aftermath and the winter calendar. Avoid April–June's punishing heat-and-humidity and the June–September monsoon, when the city floods.

rows.label: Flights from India
rows.value: Direct from Delhi (~2h10m), Mumbai (~2h40m) and Bengaluru (~2h30m) into Kolkata (CCU); Air India flies business on the Delhi/Mumbai trunk, IndiGo carries the frequency. It is also the natural gateway on to Bhutan and the Northeast, use the premium lounge, and allow time as the city-side traffic is dense.

rows.label: Health & safety
rows.value: No vaccinations beyond routine for a standard visit. A safe, walkable city with warm people; normal metro caution. No altitude. Humidity is heavy outside winter. Tap water is not potable, sealed bottled water, and be selective with street food despite the temptation.

rows.label: Dining, veg & Jain
rows.value: Good for vegetarians and workable for Jain, though Bengali cuisine leans fish-forward. The city has a strong Marwari/Gujarati community, so pure-veg and Jain kitchens are genuinely easy to find. 6 Ballygunge Place and Bhojohori Manna do fine vegetarian Bengali; Kewpie's and the veg-Jain kitchens at the Taj/ITC properties handle strict requirements well.
